title: Procurement: MSA/DPA review & SLAs - Mariner Biotech
summary: Redwood and Mariner Biotech reviewed the MSA/DPA redlines and SLA expectations for a pilot and potential enterprise onboarding. Action items include sending redlined MSA/DPA, SOC 2 package, updated pricing spreadsheet, and scheduling legal follow-up next week.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-20
Time: 15:00 - 15:55 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen, Samir Patel, Ravi Kaur (Redwood); Dr. Elena Cruz, Marcus Lee, Priya Nair, Daniel Ortiz (Mariner Biotech)

---
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick agenda — run through the MSA/DPA redlines, SLA asks, and next steps for pilot onboarding. Marcus, can you confirm procurement timeline?
[00:14] Marcus Lee: Sure, thanks Maya. We need final pricing approved by our procurement board by end of month so we can kick off the pilot in November. Legal has a few non-starters on the MSA, so that's why Daniel is on here.
[00:32] Daniel Ortiz: Yeah, mostly around indemnity and data residency. For biotech data we need guaranteed control and audit logs, and we're asking about HSM/KMS integration, encryption at rest keys managed by us.
[00:48] Samir Patel: Totally understood. Redwood's Private offering supports customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations; we can do VPC peering or on-prem nodes for air-gapped needs. There's also Dedicated capacity if you want predictable throughput without full private control.
[01:05] Priya Nair: Can you clarify difference again — Private vs Dedicated? Last doc i saw had a bit of conflation, says private is control plane separate but still uses some managed services.
[01:18] Samir Patel: Yes, sorry for the confusion — Private gives you the control plane in your VPC and can be on-prem if required; Dedicated is Redwood-managed reserved GPU pools in our infra with stronger isolation but we still control the control plane. For strict data residency and key management you want Private.
[01:35] Dr. Elena Cruz: Our primary ask is that keys never leave our KMS and that logs are forwarded to our SIEM. We also need SOC 2 evidence and audit logs retention for at least 7 years.
[01:52] Maya Chen: We can provide SOC 2 Type II and an audit pack. On retention, we typically provide configurable retention windows — i'll flag that with product but we can propose 7 years as an enterprise option.
[02:08] Marcus Lee: On SLA — for the pilot we just need 99.5% uptime and p95 latency under 600ms for text generation endpoints. For production we'll discuss 99.9% with credits.
[02:24] Samir Patel: 99.5% for pilot is doable depending on architecture. If you need sub-600ms p95, we'd recommend moving critical paths to Dedicated or Private with optimized batching and kernel selection. There's always a tradeoff between cost and latency.
[02:41] Marcus Lee: Cost is a factor — procurement is pushing back on high reserved commitments. What's the minimum commit for Dedicated?
[02:50] Maya Chen: We have monthly reserved blocks; minimums depend on GPU type. I'll include a pricing sheet with options — burst capacity and pay-as-you-go overlays. We'll also show a cost comparison between Dedicated and Private for your expected token volumes.
[03:08] Daniel Ortiz: On liability, we have a couple redlines on indemnity and data breach notification timelines — 72 hours is our requirement. Is Redwood able to commit to that?
[03:20] Maya Chen: We aim for 72 hours; for enterprise contracts we include incident response and SLA terms. We'll have Redwood legal work the specifics in the redline.
[03:33] Priya Nair: Technical question — can we run a small performance benchmark with our internal prompt sets to validate latency and cost? If so, what access is needed?
[03:44] Samir Patel: Absolutely. We'll need a test dataset, API keys for a sandbox tenant, and network peering for Private. For Dedicated we can spin a small reserved pool for the benchmark. I'll prepare a checklist: network, KMS access (if needed), sample prompt sets, expected concurrency.
[04:02] Dr. Elena Cruz: Also want to confirm data deletion processes for the pilot. We cannot have persistent KV cache of PHI outside controlled retention windows.
[04:14] Samir Patel: Understood. We have prefix/KV cache controls and can disable persistent caching or enable strict TTLs. We'll document the config.
[04:30] Marcus Lee: For procurement approvals, who needs to sign off on the pricing sheet from your side?
[04:36] Maya Chen: I'll be the AE owner and sign off commercial terms; finance will countersign and legal will be on the MSA redlines. I'll include contacts in the pricing doc.
[04:50] [Short crosstalk — background noise]
[05:12] Maya Chen: Ok, quick recap — action items and dates. Samir will send the pilot architecture by the 25th, I'll send redlined MSA/DPA, Ravi will drop SOC2 materials tomorrow, and we schedule legal-to-legal next week. Any blockers?
[05:28] Daniel Ortiz: We need to review the MSA redline internally first, expect comments by Tuesday.
[05:40] Marcus Lee: Procurement will try to accelerate, but budget sign-off is internal — i'll confirm by 10/30.
[05:52] Maya Chen: Great, we'll follow up in email with artifacts and a calendar invite for the legal call. Thanks everyone.

---
Notes/Artifacts referenced: pricing spreadsheet (link shared in chat), SOC 2 pack (to be shared), pilot architecture doc (to be shared by SE).

End of transcript.
